assurance.scope: engineering register; not a live security or compromise verdict
assurance.score_definition: weighted evidence of trust in JARVIS itself; not machine protection health

browser_privacy_veil.basis: opt-in metadata-only browser sensor (surfaces counted on use, named session-replay vendors, cross-origin pixel origins) with deterministic Veil correlation, and opt-in declarativeNetRequest rulesets for session recorders and tracking pixels that ship disabled, cannot match pages or frames, and yield to per-site exceptions (rule and logic tests under Node stubs)
browser_privacy_veil.blind_spot: No installed/attested browser integration; blocking is unvalidated in a live browser; first-party/CNAME-cloaked or server-side trackers and recorders served from the site origin are neither named nor blocked; the main-world probe can be forged or evaded by the page

input_surveillance.basis: injected-input hook with forensics, source-tested exact media-control/key-event reconciliation and proportionate media-only severity, hook-chain latency and per-interval stall episodes, pointer-setting and LowLevelHooksTimeout checks, keyboard/mouse class-filter and Scancode Map inventory, monitoring-tool process-name heuristics, screen-capture posture, and an elevated-broker Win32k AuditApiCalls trace inventorying low-level hook (1002) and background raw-input (1001) registrations by process, image and signature; the event fields and attribution were measured on 2026-09-23 with a positive control (WH_MOUSE_LL and a keyboard RIDEV_INPUTSINK both captured), and validated end to end through the scheduled broker the same day: an unelevated control that had already exited was identified from Sysmon history and reported (keyboard sink high, mouse hook medium)
input_surveillance.blind_spot: GetAsyncKeyState polling is not logged on this build (1003 absent under the positive control), so polling loggers are invisible; the trace does not survive reboot, so watchers registered before its first broker run each boot are unseen; stalls are symptoms and never attributed to a process; the input hook does not identify which process injected a media control

credential_guardian.basis: secret scanning and credential access collectors

system_state_graph.basis: ProcessGuid lineage, conservative snapshot/event reconciliation, source-tested bounded byte-and-identity checks for deleted Linux executables, deterministic posture debt and conditional remediation projections, bounded repair audit state, and repeated-sample sustained-health verification; source-tested host topology (WSL /init runtime proven by file identity, read-only mount and /init ancestry; argv0-link, shebang and systemd-helper name explanations with a system-binary collision guard; WSL-declared DNS tunnel listener), typed KNOWN_SAFE/KNOWN_UNSAFE/UNKNOWN observations with separate sensor health, and one bounded epoch-coherent re-query that keeps transient first sightings; source-tested WSL boundary snapshot (allowlisted wsl.conf/.wslconfig keys, DrvFs mounts, interop registration, Windows PATH entries, Docker socket presence) with an explicit-accept hash-chained checkpoint file that reports OFFLINE_STATE_DRIFT across a boot change, STATE_DRIFT within one, and EVIDENCE_LOST for unreadable sources; source-tested spyware and covert-process reasoning (jarvis reason): typed evidence, a deterministic hypothesis engine with exact-publisher category explanations, dual-use handling, per-mechanism blind spots and missing-evidence output, and a notes-only typed advisory; measured on a synthetic corpus of 8 spyware controls and 11 legitimate look-alikes (8 of 8 detected, 0 false positives) and on the live host with every source current; deployed live (release 686d4763a3a1); the deterministic engine additionally live-verified against real emulated mechanisms in a locked-down, non-root, no-network QEMU/KVM disposable guest (jarvis/lab/vmlab.py), 4 independent runs: 5 of 6 testable Linux positive controls detected with every expected fact present and correct latency, one honestly skipped for missing guest hardware, one clean-process guard stayed quiet every run, isolation verified each run (container removed, run directory removed, base image checksum unchanged); its own clean-guest baseline caught a real false positive on the legitimate systemd-logind daemon, fixed with a narrow path-anchored exception and confirmed clean on the next 2 runs
system_state_graph.blind_spot: No privileged live proof yet for the deleted-executable reconciliation or the topology explanations (not deployed; the service view with CAP_SYS_PTRACE has not run them); Windows interop (/init-backed .exe processes) and container execution domains are not modelled; the WSL VM-root owner of loopback udp/323 is unobservable; no complete cross-layer causal graph, broad verified remediation orchestration, reboot-cycle sustained-health proof, or long-duration soak evidence; the WSL boundary checkpoint has no accepted live baseline, no scheduled comparison, no alert wiring, no cross-boundary process edges, and its local hash chain has no independent anchor; the reasoning workflow is not scheduled; the isolated positive-control lab is Linux-only so far and on-demand rather than scheduled, and its Windows counterpart is designed but blocked on the owner enabling Windows Sandbox (not installed on this host) - the safer design uses only existing signed tools (the AutoHotkey #UseHook directive, file copy/rename), never custom hook-registration code, after a safety classifier declined raw Win32 capture-API source; corpus results are synthetic and say nothing about mechanisms no sensor observes (polling keyloggers, BitBlt or DXGI capture, clipboard listeners, who called SendInput, local staging, beacon timing, kernel-level hiding); the advisory model did not separate controls from explained look-alikes on the corpus and has no authority over verdict or depth

behavioral_physics.blind_spot: Hardware counters and robust multivariate validation incomplete

sensor_integrity.basis: native sequence/digest replay checks, manifest-addressed spool reads, process-deadlined ingestion, continuous-coverage cursors, snapshot/event perception states, live-validated elevated Sysmon policy export (2026-09-22: running config hash equals windows-sysmon/jarvis-windows-baseline.xml, ProcessCreate unfiltered), the running Sysmon configuration hash continuously compared with the reviewed baseline, fresh Windows reconciliation and an EventLogReader boot-pressure probe (2s measured through the elevated broker on 2026-09-23 over 34002 events, was a 120s timeout via Get-WinEvent); receipts, freshness budgets, leases and supervised recovery watchdogs; source-tested on-demand WSL wall-clock stability probe (paired realtime/monotonic samples plus the journal step records; measured 2026-09-30 as unstable with -2.47 s steps about every 30 s)
sensor_integrity.blind_spot: Independent authenticated sensors and anti-replay remain incomplete; boot 94 still overflowed the driver queue 46s after boot, under the previous policy, dropping 82 ProcessCreate and 64784 RegistryEvent records; the revised baseline removes 95% of registry volume in a replay of this boot (37062 to 1927 events) but is not yet applied, and whether it prevents boot-time overflow is unmeasured until it is applied and the machine reboots; no export of the pre-change policy was preserved; the clock probe is not scheduled, cannot identify the cause of a step, and detectors that compare wall-clock windows are not yet monotonic-based

continuous_attestation.blind_spot: No validated TPM quote/PCR trust chain

component_isolation.basis: fixed response action registry; capability-aware visibility checks and a detector for privileged units running user-editable code; root-owned sealed release run under python3 -I with three visibility capabilities; source-tested execution identities (Ed25519 key readable only by the capability-holding daemon, binding observed via SO_PEERCRED/pidfd, CLOCK_BOOTTIME expiry, ancestry attribution) and agent/test capsules with private TMPDIR (docs/architecture/EVIDENCE-FABRIC.md); JARVIS-managed scheduled tasks verified against one declaration table (all 9 live tasks verified against the real checkout on 2026-09-24)
component_isolation.blind_spot: Observer and responder privilege separation incomplete; execution identities are not live until a deploy provisions the key (no measured issuance yet); capsule capabilities are declared, not enforced; agent actors are self-declared; Windows-side (interop) processes are not attributed; provenance is attribution only and lowers no finding

forensic_storage.basis: authoritative Python hash-chained temporal event log plus an independently durable Rust gzip segment store with locked writers, atomic segment commits and full verification, fed by a governed bounded mirror job: events carry their authoritative source_seq, the store is its own cursor, ingest is all-or-nothing, budgeted pruning keeps the header chain and a store cursor behind the recorded one pauses mirroring as tampering evidence; an append-only Windows vault (Administrators/SYSTEM write, owner read) filled by the elevated broker and verified against the live chain (2026-09-23: 36 segments vaulted and payload-verified); OpenTimestamps anchors of the chain heads (only a 32-byte digest leaves the machine; first proof accepted by 4 calendars, Bitcoin confirmation pending); evidence cases and response intent records
forensic_storage.blind_spot: An administrator can still alter or delete the vault; anchors expose a rewrite of anchored history only while an anchor record survives somewhere and only once its Bitcoin proof exists (hours), and new events between anchors (up to 6h) are unanchored; the vault is on this machine, not off-host, and is unencrypted; the Rust mirror is not tamper-independent; retention gaps before vaulting are counted, not recoverable

temporal_correlation.basis: globally sequenced native events, multi-category temporal projection (process/network/file/registry/driver/ipc/wmi/malware/protection/task/sensor), event-consumed detectors, process lineage, incidents and snapshot reconciliation clamped to the current boot by its kernel-lifetime processes; source-tested observation epochs (boot id, wall-minus-monotonic step, kernel suspend delta, release change) with epoch-scoped monotonic ordering, recorded by the hidden job
temporal_correlation.blind_spot: Epochs are not yet consumed by Sysmon/native reconciliation, so cross-standby wall-clock comparisons there remain; Windows process reconciliation only; the sensor labels records with the boot current at read time, so the prior boot shutdown tail is excluded at reconciliation, not at ingest; kernel minimal processes (Registry, Memory Compression, vmmem) have no start event and stay unknown; attack-sequence and cross-layer coverage incomplete

performance.basis: per-subsystem scheduler duty cycle, process/RAM/database profiling, shared process/socket providers, optional Rust metrics/governance and durable-store bridge, plus hourly-validated OpenVINO GPU execution of bounded deterministic graphs (GPU.0, CPU-reference cross-checked)
performance.blind_spot: No complete measured CPU/RAM/IO/battery/latency budget, authoritative Rust sensor-ingest integration or comparative CPU-vs-GPU throughput benchmark

supply_chain.basis: standard-library Python runtime, exact-file hash check for one reviewed agent plugin version, a live service-verified exact-payload match to a Microsoft WHCP-signed Logitech DriverStore installer (2026-09-23), and a source-tested release controller: content-addressed release_id, single-writer deploy lock, --expect-base refusal of stale narrow releases, recorded installation checkout, and refusal of world-writable build sources
supply_chain.blind_spot: Signed reproducible releases, complete SBOM validation, and broader package provenance unverified; the release controller has not yet run as root on this machine (the live deploy script predates it)

recovery.basis: action undo, fresh repair observations and read-only interrupted-action reconciliation

self_improvement.basis: human-gated fix proposals: deterministic daemon scan, bounded validated Ollama directives, OpenCode patch drafting, advisory Jev assessments (Tier-2, human-gated, offline-safe), separate investigation and exact-patch authorization, test-gated apply with revert
self_improvement.blind_spot: No autonomous code execution; model directives remain untrusted, application stays human-authorized, and email replies cannot approve

producing.detail: sensor completed its last read pass
